public_rationale: Meta announced Make-A-Video on September 29, 2022, describing its output as brief, high-quality video clips [e1]. Its September 2022 paper acknowledged that the approach could not learn associations between text and phenomena inferable only from video [e2]. Neither item establishes whether the release demonstrations showed a human-handed cat, an unchanged portrait during painting, or comparable basic errors, so the observation remains unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: The original moving clips were not independently inspected in this assessment.
The evidence contains no independent confirmation or refutation of the alleged visual defects.
Meta's description of quality and its acknowledged technical limitation do not establish the quality or errors of the specific demonstrations.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Make a Video, as with AI systems before it, is caught between very impressive output and basic errors, such as giving a cat a human hand or a painting that never changes.

statement.excerpt: It’s also, as ever, stuck in the liminal space between superintelligence and super-lost.

from_speaker: MetaAI’s new text-to-movie software Make a Video
A cat holding a remote control shouldn’t have a human hand.
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that recognizable, impressive generated scenes also contain basic semantic or physical errors. The reference to superintelligence is figurative.
The target is the release demonstrations available when Marcus wrote, from September 29 through October 2, 2022.
The examples illustrate the broader observation; support need not establish that every demonstration fails. Nevertheless, a general technical limitation alone does not verify a visible error.
The phrase 'as ever' supplies rhetorical continuity, not a separately measurable claim about every earlier AI system.
criteria.support_condition: The original demonstrations, or reliable independent descriptions of them, establish recognizable generated scenes alongside basic semantic or physical errors.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable inspection establishes that the alleged defects are absent or misdescribed and that the cited demonstrations do not exhibit comparable basic errors.

evidence.explanation: Establishes the release date and the company's description of the capability. It does not independently establish quality or the alleged errors.
The authors acknowledge a gap in learning relationships specific to moving scenes. That makes Marcus's interpretation plausible but does not establish what happened in the cat or portrait clips.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Inspection across frames of the original September 29–October 2, 2022 release demonstrations, or reliable independent descriptions, establishing whether recognizable scenes contain the alleged or comparable basic errors. The assessment must distinguish intentional surreal content from unintended inconsistency.
